reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 25-35 feet of water over trees with jigs and minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in grass in 8-12 feet of water with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senkos and crankbaits. Bass are good on brush in 15-18 feet of water with spoons and Texas rig worms. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water before sunrise with small shad profile baits fished high in the water column.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Lake Bastrop schooling bass are good throwing small clear topwaters, small swimbaits in shad colors on a tiny ball jighead, underspins, a small belly weight hook, or drag a shaky head with a watermelon based color trick worm. A Carolina rigged fluke or finesse worm works great on the ledges and a frog around the reeds can land a bigger bass. There is some schooling action in the evenings, but the bass are finicky.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the mornings and evenings. Crappie are being caught in high numbers on brushpiles with minnows. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Check out the backs of coves for hydrilla and milfoil, fish patterns should draw bass out from cover. Crappie continue to congregate on structure, schooling on timber in 10-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass morning bite is good around points or pond weed with topwaters. Crappie limits are still possible but will take some time.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: However, black bass, stripers, and catfish have all been slow this week.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on dock poles and brush piles using jigs early and minnows. Fish are sluggish in the afternoon heat, Largemouth bass bite is good shallow using jigs, crankbaits, and soft plastic Texas rig baits. Hybrids are fair on points and main lake humps with slabs or live shad. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 7 pounds are good in brush in 3-20 feet of water, shoreline grass with white or green pumpkin swim jigs, crankbaits and top waters. Bass are in a summer pattern. Crappie are good with fish up to 12 inches being caught in 18-25 feet of water on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are pushing out toward main lake points, and offshore structure.
reports.by: the Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: After catching some water bass are shallow over rocks in 5-15 feet of water throwing crankbaits, swimbaits, frogs or soft plastics such as flukes, worms and craw worms. Throwing moving baits like crankbaits and jerkbaits will get a lot of bites from those and largemouth as well. Crappie are fair in 15-20 feet of water on timber with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass schooling action should improve around grass and pads with shad patterned flukes, topwater baits, buzz baits.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striper action has been slow, and black bass activity is very limited at this time.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Good go-to setups include a variety of slabs, sometimes paired with 2–3 jigs above, and the always-reliable yellow bladed jig using the proven saw tooth retrieve technique.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: At this time, all boat ramps are closed, but bank fishing can still be productive for catfish, crappie, white bass, and freshwater drum.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is fair at best, with most catches coming on soft plastics in 4-8 feet of water.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting well around the docks and offshore structure, especially on plum-colored worms in 5-25 feet of water. Crappie fishing has been fair in 13-23 feet, with hair jigs outperforming plastics, and minnows working best–if you can keep the bream and bluegill off them. Hybrids and white bass are active on flats and drop-offs in 18-32 feet, hitting slabs, spoons, and live bait.
reports.by: Bradley, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: As the summer temperatures increase the water temperature target crappie are in deeper timber along the river channel, and brush piles.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Corpus Christi Lake fishing report
reports.text: They were targeting bass specifically, but noted the wind made it tough to stay on the fish.
reports.by: Weber’s Landing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: The shallow bass bite is slowing as the water temperature reaches the 90s. Bass are 20 feet of water biting deep diving crankbaits, shaky heads and Carolina rigs. Some bass are moving offshore, so a jig or a Carolina rig will get a lot of bites. A frog or a topwater early will get some nice bass blowing up on those.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: There is a good morning bass bite around pond weed and grass with topwater baits and flukes. Bass are good in front of the weeds with chatterbaits and spinnerbaits in 3-5 feet. Fish this type of cover at midday when bass are seeking cover. Drop a clouser on an isolated cover for black bass. Lake Fork crappie fishing is improving as we enter the summer pattern.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are slow on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth are good to 7 pounds on spinnerbaits, lipless crankbaits and soft plastics worked in clearer water in sloughs and creeks on many areas of the lake. Crappie are slow, but the best reports are coming from fishing structure mid-lake with small minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 4 pounds in 3-5 feet of water. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows fished in shallow brush piles. White bass are good on slab spoons fished on roadbeds and ridges.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: However, areas in the south end of the lake, off the beaten path, offer better water clarity and solid opportunities for largemouth bass, with grubs on 3/16 ounce weight and spinnerbaits producing well. Bass are grouping up near drains and deeper pockets in narrow channels. Crappie are also scattered but can be found tight to structure in 8-14 feet of water is Luces Bayou and the East Fork.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good around docks and shallow grass throwing a frog around the grass and big rocks.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting on soft plastics and jigs in brush, and schoolers are biting swimbaits and rattletraps

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be found shallow during the early morning hours before the sun rises on topwaters and small soft plastics Texas rigged. Larger slot fish and occasional oversized bass are in this depth range. Crappie are out on your favorite summer deep spots on minnows.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: The gates are open releasing water so the crappie bite is all over the place. Crappie can be caught in 7-9 feet of water on laydowns, or on deep piles in 25 feet. If fish are not surfacing use a 1 ounce white slab.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows in 16-20 feet of water on brush piles. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on docks and bulkheads in 3-10 feet of water skipping a light jig or Texas-rigged fluke or worm. Bass are good around submerged grass on a chatterbaits and a Texas rig worm, or around brush piles and rock piles dragging a worm.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are slow to fair on points and humps in 15-32 feet of water with slabs, spoons, spinnerbaits and live bait. Crappie are fair in 15-28 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, and submerged cover near drop-offs with minnows and jigs. Largemouth bass can be caught shallow around bushes and rock in 5 feet of water. Hybrid striper 20-30 feet of water near creek channels with live bait or slabs. Crappie are on main lake brush in 15-20 feet of water or cruising deep hard bottom flats.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 10-18 feet of water on power lines, standing timber, or offshore brush with minnows. White bass are in 7-17 feet of water with slabs. Largemouth bass are good in 4-14 feet of water with boat docks, bulkheads, and rocks with chatterbaits, Texas rigs, Carolina rigs, and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair along the hydrilla with frogs, swimbaits and Texas rigged wacky worms. Crappie are fair to good with larger schools showing up in brush and standing timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in 10 feet of water along grass lines biting big Carolina rigged worms and dropshots. Crappie are excellent on main lake stumps over 22 feet of water.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass are suspended in 8 feet of water, with some bigger fish being caught off the bottom in 8-10 feet. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on Carolina rigs and deep diving crankbaits. Cast a spook of popper into schooling bass. Crappie are excellent in 15-20 feet of water on stumps or on shallow brush piles.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 9 pounds possible. Main lake bass are in 12-22 feet of water scoping minnows around bait. Crappie reports are finally improving. Crappie can be caught with minnows around brush in 8-15 feet of water or suspended over timber.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush in 14 feet of water with minnows, or in timber in 18-25 feet of water with jigs. Bass are good in 4-7 feet of water with senkos.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and sand bass are very slow.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on grass and deep trees with Carolina rigs or deep diving medium ces boats. Crappie are fair and scattered with primarily smaller sized fish being caught on white and chartreuse 1/16-1/32 ounce crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Target bass in brush piles with big worms and deep diving crank baits.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is fair, and the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait and bluegill are fair on crickets or worms. Crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water. Black bass are slow on crankbaits and shiny spinnerbaits in 2-8 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling up in the mornings in the trees behind the island and some off church hump.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth and smallmouth are improving with the lake conditions and water clarity. Smallmouth will be on the boulders and rocks off the banks in 8-15 feet of water. Largemouth will shade and suspend in the clearer water under docks and marinas.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is holding steady, with a solid shallow water bite early in the morning and again during midday. Crappie fishing has slowed with the heat and high water, with the best reports coming from anglers fishing at night under lighted docks or using floating flood lights–live bait is outperforming jigs.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of bass are down, but the grass and ledges are still producing the most. Small swimbaits on underspins are catching schooling bass. Summer marina fishing continues in 30-40 feet of water for bass, white bass, crappie and bluegill. Grass action for bass has slowed.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 10-15 feet of water with live bait over artificials. Bass up to 6 pounds are suspended on structure in 20-25 feet of water on shad colored crankbaits, or a senkos. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Successful techniques for bass include moving baits like crankbaits, spinnerbaits, jerkbaits, and chatterbaits.
reports.by: the long-time running tournament established in 2013

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 8-12 feet of water in grass with Texas rigged worms, wacky rigged senkos, and crankbaits. Bass are also good on brush in 15-18 feet of water with spoons and Texas rig worms. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling up in the mornings in the discharge. There is some schooling action in the evenings, but the bass are finicky.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is good on small jigs and minnows. Largemouth bass are good off points on hard plastics, soft plastics and live bait.
reports.by: Hundley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding actively in a summer pattern. Crappie are great in 20 feet of water on minnows. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Check out the backs of coves for hydrilla and milfoil, fish patterns should draw bass out from cover. Crappie are congregating on structure and as water temperatures climb to the upper 80s fish will remain in this pattern. Crappie are schooling on timber in 10-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early in the morning around shallow bushes and main lake pockets with topwaters like frogs and buzz baits. Crappie are excellent on timber from 15-30 feet of water with hair jigs tipped with minnows.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is fair on dock poles and brush piles. Largemouth bass bite is decent shallow using jigs, crankbaits, and soft plastic Texas rig baits. White bass topwater bite is on and hybrids are good on points and main lake humps with slabs or live shad. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4.50 pounds are good in 3-15 feet of water on Hag’s swim jigs in white or green pumpkin and topwaters. Bass are in a summer pattern with some schooling on flats and points. Crappie are good to 16 inches on minnows and jigs in 18-25 feet of water on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and at the 279 Bridge.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: After catching some water bass are shallow over rocks in 5-15 feet of water throwing crankbaits, swimbaits, frogs or soft plastics such as flukes, worms and craw worms. Throwing moving baits like crankbaits and jerkbaits will get a lot of bites from those and largemouth as well. Crappie are fair in 15-20 feet of water on minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Some bass can be caught on trees with big worms, senkos and top water baits.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Use slabs on drop-offs and along seawalls early in the mornings in depth of 5-14 feet. Reports of great catches using silver or white slabs and spinners and retrieving off the bottom at a very slow retrieve to catch these fish in depths of 17-26 feet of water. The crappie have also migrated back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: A few white bass and crappie are being caught as well.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Channel catfish, bass, and crappie are hitting on minnows.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 2 pounds are slow in 10-20 feet of water around the lake off points with a scope minnow. Crappie are excellent to 14 inches on minnows in 8-15 feet under docks in Rattlesnake Cove on the right side going in.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fish are fair.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing had been good on wind blown points, around bream beds, and near structure in 5-25 feet of water. Crappie action has been fair, with catches coming from 13 to 23 feet using jigs. Hybrids and white bass have been productive using slabs, spoons, crankbaits, and live bait.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding actively in a summer pattern. Crappie are great in 20 feet of water on minnows. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Crappie are excellent on brush piles and docks but you will have to weed through numbers of small fish to catch a limit.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with bass assassins early morning around rocks, or under the lights at nights with chrome and blue rattletraps, or bucktail jigs. Crappie are fair on deep water brush piles and docks with jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on shallow points early then moving deep to a summer depth in 14-20 feet of water hitting deep diving crankbaits, shaky heads and Carolina rigs. Some bass are moving offshore, so a jig or a Carolina rig will get a lot of bites. A frog or a topwater early will get some nice bass blowing up on those.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good mid morning with shaky heads, and crankbaits on points with 1.5-2.5 square bills in 3-5 feet around bream beds. Fish this type of cover at midday when bass are seeking cover. Drop a clouser on an isolated cover for black bass. Lake Fork crappie fishing is getting better and better as we get deeper into the summer pattern.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service.Lily fields are filling in, hydrilla and…

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs in shade and brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow feeding on shad in shallow water. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in the back of the creeks where the water has settled out some. Crappie are slow to fair in the muddy water holding close to structures.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good all over the lake in areas with shallow cover in 3-6 feet of water. Crappie are good in 5-10 feet of water on jigs tipped with minnows.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good showing up in better schools on humps in 27 feet of water hitting slabs.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: White bass and largemouth bass are stacking up in the drains, especially in narrow canals, and are hitting a variety of baits including grubs, crankbaits, and spinnerbaits. Crappie, on the other hand, have been tough to find due to strong wind current.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with mostly undersized catches with a few good stringers. Crappie are on brush piles biting minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good are around docks and rocks in 5-12 feet of water with jigs, Texas-rigged soft plastics, and a topwater frog is getting some big bites.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great on blue and chartreuse crankbaits early in the morning and late afternoon ranging from 10-15 feet of water. Crappie are good on slip cork minnows with fish suspended 10-12 feet down over timber in 20 feet of water.
reports.by: Brian Vickery Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 20 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on docks and bulkheads in 3-10 feet of water skipping a light jig or Texas-rigged fluke or worm.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.text: White bass are fair on points and humps in 15-32 feet of water with slabs, spoons, spinnerbaits and live bait. Crappie are fair in 8-28 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, and submerged cover near drop-offs with minnows and jigs.
