Crappie are on main lake brush in 15-20 feet of water or cruising deep hard bottom flats.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good skipping docks, and on ledges in 10-20 feet of water with jigs. Some bass can be targeted up river with crankbaits, frogs and plastic worms.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good along the hydrilla with Texas rigged worms, weightless senco’s and small swim baits. Crappie are fair and it seems fish have scattered into smaller schools suspended in standing timber and brush piles in 20-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Hambone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: White jerkbaits have been effective for both largemouth and smallmouth bass. Crappie are also biting well, with Rosie red minnows being the top choice.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have improved to fair in 3-4 feet of water. Bass are good pitching creature baits and plastic worms shallow and hardwoods.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good Carolina rigged craw baits and deep diving crankbaits. Crappie are excellent on standing timber and deep brush piles on small chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass are stacking up in suspended mode, at about 8 feet, over taller water. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are fair on straight tailed worms and Carolina rigged craw baits. Crappie are excellent on standing timber and small brush piles with 1/32-1/16 ounce white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on brush piles hitting jigs or minnows. Largemouth bass are slow.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 9 pounds possible. Target bass with bladed jigs in green pumpkin are good in 5-8 feet of water, or on timber in 10-15 feet of water with 10 inch red bug or plum worms. Crappie are suspended 5-8 feet down around isolated timber in 25 feet of water.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in deep water on minnows. Very few reports of bass, hybrids and sand bass.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on straight tailed worms and Carolina rigged craw baits. Crappie are fair on sanding timber and small brush piles in 15-25 feet of water on small white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are related to brush piles in 12-18 feet of water. Crappie are showing up at bridge columns and moving around drop-offs going from structure to structure.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: You can now start flipping shallow for bass. Largemouth bass are offshore in 18-25 feet of water primarily on rock piles with 10 inch worms, crankbaits and football jigs. A few bass on timber at dawn and dusk weightless flukes or weightless senkos. Mayfly hatch is going on so the best crappie bite is at first light. Crappie are scattered and slow after the recent rain. Crappie are good in brush piles and timber in 18-25 feet of water. Sand bass are on humps and points in 25-40 feet of water with slabs. Dan’s Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan’s Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action is slow. Even though we are approaching summer there are still a lot of shallow bass.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are shallow early in the pencil and hay grass with topwater baits. Then bass move to points and drains with Carolina rigs and jigs. Crappie are slowly moving to brush piles, with a better bite on the south end of the lake and Ash Bayou.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is fair, and the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. Crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water. Black bass are fair on crankbaits and shiny spinnerbaits in 2-8 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Target newly flooded cattails for bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Topwater action on "schoolie" largemouth increased this past week but is far from peaking. Bass are schooling up on the main lake so be ready with some walking baits and other topwaters to catch quite a few that way.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Best baits have been live Shad and slab spoons. Crappie are decent. Largemouth bass are good on shallow structures such as submerged irrigation intakes near docks, rip rap and shallow lay downs and brush piles.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow due to the conditions. Bass will be slow until the water clears.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is still good. Crappie fish has been a little off lately due to the big storms over the past week. The rising water and strong winds have made it tough, as crappie do not typically like those conditions.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Time to fish marinas in 30-40 feet of water for bass, white bass, crappie and bluegill. Grass action for bass has slowed.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: White bass and crappie are biting at night under lights with minnows or shad.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles and standing timber in 10-20 feet of water with live bait or light blue artificials. Bass up to 6 pounds are suspended on structure in 20-25 feet of water on shad colored crankbaits, or a senkos. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught in deeper water with crankbaits and Carolina rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on small jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Hundley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are loaded on the brush piles in all depths hitting jigs. Bass are in a summer pattern biting early morning and late night around lights. Lots of spotted bass and yellow bass are being caught right now too. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Check out the backs of coves for hydrilla and milfoil, fish patterns should draw bass out from cover. Crappie are excellent schooling on timber in 10-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite is good on points and flats with bushes using weedless topwaters, buzzbaits and popping frogs. There is a good bass bite in pond weed with popping or walking frogs 1-4 feet. Crappie are excellent on timber from 15-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is fair on dock poles and brush piles. Largemouth bite is decent shallow using jigs, crankbaits, and soft plastic texas rig baits, the white bass topwater bite is on and hybrids are good on points and main lake humps with slabs or live shad. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 6.19 pounds are good in 3-25 feet of water on spinnerbaits and topwaters. Bass have moved into an early summer pattern with some schooling in small wolf packs. Crappie are good to 12 inches on minnows and jigs in 18-25 feet of water on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: It is a shad bite right now for main lake bass, so focus on grass or lily pad clumps with shad. Tree bass are being caught on senkos, big worms, frogs and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Focus on drop-offs and along seawalls early in the mornings in 5-14 feet of water with slabs. Reports of great catches in 17–26 feet of water using silver or white slabs and spinnerbaits off the bottom with a very slow retrieve. The crappie have also migrated back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and a few bass are being caught off the bank.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 2 pounds are good in 10-20 feet of water around the lake off points with a minnow. Crappie are excellent to 14 inches on minnows in 8-15 feet under docks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair at 2-8 feet.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good on wind blown points, bream beds and structure from 5-25 feet. Crappie have been fair at best when you can find them. Hybrids and white bass are on flats and drop-offs in 16-34 feet of water using live large goldfish or minnows, slabs, spoons, and crankbaits.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10-20 feet of water on timber and brush piles.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are loaded on the brush piles in all depths hitting jigs. Bass are in a summer pattern biting early morning and late night around lights. Lots of spotted bass and yellow bass are being caught right now too. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Crappie are excellent on brush piles and docks but you will have to weed through numbers of small fish to catch a limit.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are good in 25 feet of water with chartreuse and white slabs with a fle fly. Crappie are good on deep water brush piles with jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on the points early then moving deep to a summer depth in 20-30 feet of water hitting deep diving crankbaits, shaky heads and Carolina rigs.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite is good on main lake points with topwaters. Fish this type of cover at midday when bass are seeking cover. Drop a clouser on an isolated cover for black bass. Crappie fishing on Lake Fork is heating up just like the temperatures. White crappie are in timber and brush piles. Black crappie are loaded up on rock piles, tire reefs, brush piles, laydowns, underwater bridges, road beds, docks and regular bridges. Crappie are still biting minnows, hand tied jigs and soft plastics. Reports of some crappie biting larger bass baits when anglers are fishing in areas with a large concentration of bigger crappie. It is a great time to get out and load the cooler with some tasty slabs.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on plastic worms fished in shallow water. Crappie are good on minnows fished over brush piles in 7-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good using worms and grubs Texas rigged and recently being caught with deep diving crank baits. White bass are being caught on the humps by the dam on little Georges and duck tracker slabs vertical jigging. Crappie are fantastic, but you have to get them early as the bite does not last long in the morning. Crappie are tight to structure in 6-10 feet of water eating small hand tied jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on soft plastics and jigs around docks and brush out to 14 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught shallow, mid depths, and deep. Crappie can still be caught using crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are still good on main lake points and bridges. Look for large bait balls on your graph and the white bass and largemouth bass will be close by. Crappie are starting to stack up on standing timber and brush piles 12-20 feet of water. Crappie are starting to prefer minnows over jigs.
reports.by: Brian Vickery Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 18-24 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on docks and bulkheads in 3-10 feet of water skipping a light jig or Texas-rigged fluke or worm.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on points and humps in 15-32 feet of water with slabs, spoons, spinnerbaits and live bait. Crappie are fair in 8-28 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, and submerged cover near drop-offs with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good along the edge of hydrilla with Texas rigged worms and small swimbaits. Crappie are good suspended in brush piles in 25-30 feet of water using minnows, or imitation minnows with �¼ ounce jig heads.
reports.by: Hambone guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair on glide, baits, and bladed jigs up shallow. Crappie are excellent on standing timber and brush piles in like 15-25 feet of water deep piles.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass are suspended 8 feet down over deeper water biting jerkbaits plus 1. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on dropshots and Carolina rigs on grassy points. Crappie are excellent on standing timber and small brush piles with white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slower on brush piles hitting jigs or minnows. Largemouth bass are good around the docks with some mainlake.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 10 pounds possible in 5-15 feet of water. Crappie are fair on a variety of minnows and small red and white jig heads suspended in 5-15 feet of water.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair on dropshots, Carolina rigs on points. Crappie are good on sanding timber and small brush piles in 15-25 feet of water on crappie jigs. and Catfish are poor on cut bait.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are relating to brush piles in 12-18 feet of water. Crappie are showing up at bridge columns and moving around drop-offs going from structure to structure.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered and slow after the recent rain. Crappie are good in brush piles and timber in 18-25 feet of water. Largemouth bass are offshore in 18-25 feet of water primarily on rock piles with 10 inch worms, crankbaits and football jigs. A few bass on timber at dawn and dusk weightless flukes or weightless senkos. Sand bass are on humps and points in 25-40 feet of water with slabs. Dan’s Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan’s Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action is slow. Black bass are fair using deep crankbaits, jigs, and dragging plastics. Be sure to target bass on stump rows, rock piles, and brush piles.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: The first few "schoolie" largemouth are beginning to show up on topwater; this is very light and very scattered, but should continue to get more common and widespread as we get into summer.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing will improve as the lake clears up and the fish move to summer patterns with warmer water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles with minnows and jigs in 10-16 feet of water. Bass are scattered with a fair topwater bite or feeler with trick worms, spinnerbaits and topwaters. Crappie have been in two main patterns with most fish 20 feet deep, but there is a good number of fish in 8-12 feet of water on brush piles. Bass are great at dawn and dusk on topwater, but this bite shuts off very quickly.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on fire in the summer pattern hanging out in 10-18 feet of water on structures. Minnows always work well, but a purple crappie jig with a chartreuse tail is a good artificial. Black bass are suspended over structure in 20 feet of water hitting crankbaits or a silver spoon. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 25-40 feet on jigs and minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs moving deeper midday.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass continue to be shallow, or on deep points with crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 8-12 feet of water in grass with Texas rigged worms, wacky rigged senkos, and crankbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are deep around bait and setting up on brush piles.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling up in the mornings in the discharge. A good summertime pattern is to target bass dragging the bottom with Alabama rigs in 20 feet of water.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with hard plastics off ledges, and soft plastics around brush.
reports.by: Hundley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are loaded on the brush piles in all depths and are doing great on jigs. Bass are in a summer pattern biting early morning and late night around lights. Lots of spotted bass and yellow bass are being caught right now too. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Check out the backs of coves for hydrilla and milfoil, fish patterns should draw bass out from cover. Crappie are excellent in timber and brush piles in 14-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite has picked up. Crappie are excellent on structure from 15-25 feet of water.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Redfish can be caught with gold and silver spoons, or imitation shad. a variety of colors from bass assassin plastics, or trolling soft plastics.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4.97 pounds are good in 8-25 feet of water on shaky heads, Hag’s Jigs or Tornados and topwaters. Bass have moved into an early summer pattern. Crappie are excellent with catches up to 15 inches on minnows and jigs in 18-25 feet of water main lake brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: White bass continue to bite on slabs and soft plastics 20-36 feet of water on wind-blown points and humps. Bigger bass are being caught on rock piles in 5-15 feet on jigs, swimbaits and most Texas-rigged soft plastics. The topwater bite is starting to turn on as well and you can catch some big bass throwing around rocky points and shallow ledges. Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The pad and grass bass are starting to heat up with flukes, ribbits, buzzbaits, frogs and such. As the lake level falls expect bass to hold tight to trees hitting big worms, senkos, flukes or frogs.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Focus drop-offs and along seawalls early in the mornings in 5-14 feet with slabs. Reports of great catches using silver or white slabs and spinners and retrieving off the bottom at a very slow retrieve to catch these fish in depths of 17-26 feet of water. The crappie have also migrated back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Some crappie and freshwater drum are being caught off the bank.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are being caught in 10 feet of water.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair, mostly on soft plastic.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to poor as they have been hit hard this spring. Largemouth bass are good on the edges, docks as well as offshore structure during the day. Hybrids and white bass are on flats and drop-offs in 14-26 feet of water using live large goldfish or minnows, slabs, spoons, and crankbaits.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10-20 feet of water on timber.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are loaded on the brush piles in all depths and are doing great on jigs. Bass are in a summer pattern biting early morning and late night around lights. Lots of spotted bass and yellow bass are being caught right now too. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Crappie are congregating on boat docks and brush piles.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair to good green and white slabs on deep water humps, points and ridges. Crappie are slow to fair on minnows around docks and deep water brush piles.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: The early morning bass bite is starting to slow. Bass are good with underspins, rattle traps and spinnerbaits in less than 4 feet of water. Bass are still not suspending.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The early morning bass bite is good on points and around grass with topwaters, and chatterbaits. Fish this type of cover at midday when bass are seeking cover. Drop a clouser on an isolated cover for black bass. Lake Fork crappie fishing improves daily as we head into the summer pattern. Crappie are on underwater bridges, underwater roadbeds, bridges, lay downs, brush piles, tire reefs and of timber in the 14-32 feet range.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow feeding on shad in shallow water. Crappie are good on brush in 14 feet of water with minows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Bigger striped bass are being taken on 1ounce slabs and live shad fished mainly on the lower ends from Decordova to near the pump stations close to the dam. Smaller stripers and sand bass are easily being caught on slabs and spinnerbaits all over the lake from Bentwater to Blue Water Shores. Largemouth bass are good to 6 pounds on soft plastics and lipless crankbaits fished in the back of sloughs and near main lake points. Crappies are holdings to structure near deeper docks, underwater timber and near bridge pilings and are good on small minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on spinnerbaits fished around cover. Crappie are good to 2 pounds on minnows fished over brush piles.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Use inline spinners shallow and slabs in deeper water.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Bass should start schooling in deeper water hitting Carolina rigs and crankbaits. Crappie should be on brush piles biting jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has improved in all depths. Crappie are moving out to the deeper cover for summer.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on main lake points, submerged bridges and road beds with shad colored crankbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie are good on standing timber and brush piles ranging 12-15 feet with slip cork jigs in blue and chartreuse and shad colors.
reports.by: Brian Vickery Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: If you are not getting bit within the first 30 minutes of sunlight, you will probably have to move out to 10-20 feet of water and use 1 ounce white or chartreuse slabs. While the gates are opening and closing the crappie bite is hit-or-miss. Black bass are biting white and chartreuse spinnerbaits in the morning around the rip wrap, concrete and shallow submerged brush on points and secondary points. Bass are not biting at the back of the coves anymore.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 18-24 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on docks and bulkheads in 3-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 10-18 feet of water on power lines, standing timber, or offshore brush with minnows. White bass are in 7-17 feet of water with super slabs. Largemouth bass are good in 4-14 feet of water with boat docks, bulkheads, and rocks with chatterbaits, Texas rigs, Carolina rigs, and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass remain good along the edge of hydrilla with Texas rigged worms. Crappie have loaded up on brush piles in 20-30 feet with minnows and pintail jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair on bladed jigs and swim jigs around shallow grass points. Crappie are good on main lake timber and brush piles in the creeks.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass are suspended 8 feet down over deeper water biting jerkbaits plus 1. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are good on Carolina rigs or medium diving crankbaits on main lake points. Crappie are excellent on main lake timber utilizing forward facing sonar.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to stack up in deeper brush piles hitting jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 10 pounds on a variety of baits in 8-18 feet of water. Some fish still targeted scoping on main lake with crappie imitation baits. Crappie starting to pick up around bigger trees suspended 5-8 feet.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass bite is good to very good on topwater and crankbaits. Crappie bite is steady with schools being located using forward facing sonar and caught using the Bone Head jigs.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush and timber in 12-22 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting in deep water on minnows.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on large swimbaits and dropshots. Crappie are fair on standing timber with small crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are related to brush piles 12-18 feet of water. Crappie are showing up at bridge columns, and moving around drop-offs going from structure to structure.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are stacking up on timber, bridge pylons and brush piles in 20-25 feet of water. Largemouth bass are moving to offshore rock piles and main lake points. Some bass can be targeted on shallow laydowns or shaded areas. Sand bass are on humps and points in 30-50 feet of water with slabs. Dan’s Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan’s Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: A slab and jig combination is hard to beat. Crappie action is slow. Black Bass are fair, with the water stained.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is fair, and the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water. Black bass are fair on crankbaits and shiny spinnerbaits in 2-8 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: Black bass catches have been improving greatly. Reports of bass caught exceeding 5 pounds, with many in the 2-3 pound range.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, swimbaits and live bait are working best. Crappie are decent on bridge pilings and shallower brush in 8-14 feet. Largemouth bite is good.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Striped bass are hit-or-miss with slabs in 15-30 feet of water, with a better bite on live bait.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good. A few great reports of 7 pound bass being caught at night with spinnerbaits, and buzzbaits along the edge of the flooded grass. Crappie are good on brush piles, standing timber, and main lake docks with jigs or live bait. The water temperature is starting to reach the mid to low 80s, pushing crappie out of the creeks.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are on the verge of schooling up as the water temperatures rise into the 80s. Look for grass on the channel swings on the main lake for a lot of bass. Some of the bigger bass are on the deeper outer side especially in the isolated patches of grass. There are some good bass on the deeper ledges as well in 15-30 feet of water. Time to fish marinas in 30-40 feet of water for bass, white bass, crappie and bluegill. Grass action for bass has slowed.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: White bass and crappie can be caught under the lights at night with minnows or shad.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles with minnows and jigs in 10-16 feet of water. Bass are scattered with a fair topwater bite or feeler with trick worms, spinnerbaits and topwaters. Bass are great with a phenomenal topwater bite the first hour of fishable light, but will shut off quickly as the sun rises. Crappie are holding in 10-20 feet on brush.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on fire in the summer pattern hanging out in 10-18 feet of water on structure. Minnows always work well but a purple crappie jig with a chartreuse tail is a good artificial. Black bass are suspended over structure in 20 feet of water hitting crankbaits or a silver spoon. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass are slow on soft plastics or crankbaits in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving into brush piles and structure setting up in a summer pattern.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good with catches up to 6 pounds on main lake points with wood, ledges, steep chunk rock banks. Watch for birds chasing bait balls, bass are schooling on the surface.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Reports of crappie catches at the oil derrick.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has settled in the normal summer pattern with the best bite early or late in the day. Bass are fair on the outside of grass lines in 8-12 feet of water with shaky heads, topwater frogs. Crappie are fair at night with minnows in 25 feet of water on brush.
reports.by: Jim Brack, Athens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early in the morning in shallow water on small swimbaits, plastic worms and topwaters.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake B.A. Steinhagen fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on soft plastics in the cuts, or with frogs over grass. Crappie are good with jigs in flooded timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in deeper water in 18 feet of water using minnows. Largemouth bass are good using soft plastics.
reports.by: Benbrook Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles and standing timber in 25-30 feet of water with jigs or minnows. Largemouth bass are good on chatterbaits and creature baits. Black bass should be receptive to topwater frogs in shad or bream patterns, and clouser type baits around grass and retaining walls. Bass are fair with fish in transitioning to deeper water summer patterns.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on early morning topwaters like frogs and choppos on grassy points.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs around offshore brush piles, deeper water docks and the U.S. Largemouth bass fishing has been tough, the best bite has been on topwater baits early in the day. Try a slab deep to pick off the hybrids under the sandies.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 6.42 pounds are good on Hag’s green pumpkin tungsten tsunami jigs, shaky heads and topwaters in 2-10 feet of water. Crappie to 14 inches are good around docks on minnows and jigs in 10-15 feet of water. White bass are fair on crankbaits and crappie jigs with some topwater action early and late.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on rock piles with topwaters, swimbaits and crankbaits. Crappie are good with crappie jigs or roadrunners.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is starting to heat up now that the water level has fallen to just above normal levels for this time of year and the clarity is improving.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair fishing along weed lines with plastic lures.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass have a decent morning topwater bite on a spook or buzzbait.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Cast spinnerbaits and slabs and look for schooling fish close to seawalls and shorelines. Use spinnerbaits like a mepps #4 spinner or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. The crappie bite has been improving now that the water is receding. Target crappie with small jigs in 5-12 feet under bridge pylons or under docks.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Target bass in 5-12 feet using soft plastic worms, shad colored or chartreuse and black medium crankbaits. Crappie are good in brush piles in 20-30 feet of water on minnows or grubs.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass offshore bite has been slow when there is no wind, but there are many of dock fish to be caught. Crappie are in or around structure 12-21 feet using minnows or jigs.
reports.by: Roy Crush IV Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20 feet of water on electric chicken jigs, and minnows. Bass are fair with fish in transitioning to deeper water summer patterns.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 8-20 feet of water on hard bottoms with plastic worms and crankbaits. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on Carolina rigs in 12-18 feet of water on redbug and watermelon red soft plastics. Bass are fair along road beds with crankbaits, jigs, Texas-rigged worms and craws and Carolina-rigged finesse worms.
reports.by: Bob Green, Bob Green Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has slowed down some as the Texas heat settles in. Black bass are chasing topwater patterns early in the day and later in the day when it is dark. Check out the brush piles as big bass are using them to feed on crappie. Lake Fork crappie fishing continues to be excellent going into the dog days of summer. Look for crappie holding on brush piles, summer time trees, lay downs, bridges and docks. One of the biggest keys to loading the boat with crappie has been finding the fish that haven’t been pressured as much. Soft plastics will work on the more aggressive crappie too.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on topwaters along the rocks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Particularly dense, isolated stands of hydrilla typically hold largemouth bass, out to the 20 foot mark. Some light topwater schooling activity has begun to occur as white bass and small largemouth school up and feed on young of the year shad they are pushing to the surface.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie moving out to deeper brush good on minnows and jigs. Bass are deep but some are very shallow in the cattails. Bass are feeding early and later.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair to good with 6 pound catches on soft plastics and deep diving crankbaits worked near main lake points and humps. Crappie fishing is good on small minnows or crappie jigs worked on submerged timber from Water’s Edge to Decordova.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow. Crappie are good on minnows and Insane plastic jigs fished in 8-16 feet of water. White bass are good on slab spoons fished over main lake humps.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greenbelt fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in standing timber. Largemouth bass are good.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are patterning up on structure shallow early and in the shade around docks and drop-offs late being caught on worms, grubs and crankbaits. Crappie are being caught on small jigs tight to structure in 8-14 feet of water in Luces Bayou and the East Fork. White bass are schooling up at the mouths of rivers and will be headed south very soon being caught on slabs and swim baits.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are hitting square bill crankbaits or shaky heads on docks, and swim jigs in shallow water around vegetation. Crappie are on minnows around standing timber and offshore brush in 8-14 feet.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 16-25 feet in standing timber with minnows on a cork. Several catches of white bass while targeting crappie. Bass are good in the bushes along the banks pitching Texas rigged worms and jigs, or wacky rigs. Bass are good on brush piles on points on the south end of the lake in 18-20 feet of water with deep running crankbaits, jigs, wacky worms and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered in 10-30 feet of water. There is a specific lift you sometimes need to do a lot when crappie fishing, it is basically playing keep away with the fish on live scope. When sandies are on the move use 3-4 inch swimbaits, otherwise 1 ounce slabs will be good. Black bass are on submerged and flooded brush with worms, senkos, white and chartreuse spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 16-22 feet of water on brush piles in jigs or minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good fishing down the dam with crankbaits and shaky head rigged worms in either redbug or watermelon red. Crappie have grouped together in deep brush and at railroad trestle on minnows.
reports.by: Hambone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on chartreuse deep diving crankbaits, or Carolina rigs in 15-20 feet of water. Crappie are excellent on brush piles with live minnows or chartreuse colored crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on dropshot and large swimbaits. Crappie are slow on live minnows.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 10 pounds. Crappie fishing is improving in the river around hardwoods in 12-18 feet.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Some crappie guides are seeing the fish move out of the deeper water returning to 8-12 feet areas to feed.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shaded areas. Crappie are very slow.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with large glide baits and 3 inch shad colored swimbaits. Crappie are slow on live minnows on standing timber and brush piles. Largemouth are heavily schooling.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are slow in 20-30 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs in white, or silver. Bass are tough in 20-35 feet of water on Texas rigged worms, deep diving crankbaits, Carolina rigs, dropshots, and shaky heads. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting good on worms and topwater lures in the early morning hours. Crappie are good on grubs and crappie bites fished near the bottom at prairie branch pier.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: There has not been any early morning schooling but expect this to start within the next week.Crappie are good in 18-28 feet of water relating to brush.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair with slabs on main lake points and humps in 15-20 feet of water. Crappie are slow on minnows over brush piles in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Summer bite is just around the corner when we will see the bass draw to deeper water points and white bass schooling. Bass are good on topwaters, or flipping soft plastics into submerged brush and points, or deeper humps and points with Carolina rigs. Crappie are in 12-16 feet of water, 20-30 feet on timber and brush. Largemouth bass are good on submerged main lake points and ledges in 16-24 feet of water with crankbaits, jig head minnow or Carolina rig.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie, bluegill and catfish are fair at the Somerville Marina. Crappie are fair on jigs and minnow, over brush, 10-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught in brush along shorelines in 4-12 feet with soft plastics.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are tough as fish seek clear water hitting buzz baits, spinnerbaits or flipping creatures or stick baits. Catfish and crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is decent fishing brush piles in creek channels 12-18 feet of water seeing a lot of fish but they are gorging on smaller shad right now and harder to catch. Bass fishing is slow fishing top waters early on main lake points. Striped bass are good on slabs in deeper water. Box fish can be caught on the surface with swimbaits and small slabs.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Guadaliupe bass can be caught on bluff walls between marinas. Bass are very active chasing shad in the marinas. Bass are good in the shaded areas of the marinas biting small swimbaits, and slowly working small topwaters. Continue to downsize baits to match the small 1 inch baitfish the bass are feeding on. Bass are schooling up early with a good bite on small belly weighted straight tail swimbaits in shad colors, walk the dog style topwater lures, jerkbaits and spoons.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with many undersized catches using minnows and jigs on brush in 16 feet of water. Bass are good on crankbaits, plastic worms and topwater frogs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on topwater frogs and worms early in the day. Most bass are in 10-25 feet of water with some schooling almost every trip.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on brush piles with jigs and minnows. Bass are slow on deeper water ledges with crankbaits and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-25 feet of water over brush with minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good 2-5 pounds in 10-30 feet of water on main lake points, near submerged trees and brush structures. Crappie fair.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good around grass banks with topwaters, and on chatterbaits, crankbaits and Texas-rigs around dock and rocks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting from first light to the early morning. Lady Bird Lake continues to be good for bass.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Lake Bastrop is still going strong with schooling bass in the discharge early and later out from and close to the north end of the dam.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in deep water with live minnows. Bass are being caught in 15-20 feet of water on soft plastics in the shallows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles and standing timber in 25-30 feet of water with jigs or minnows. Largemouth bass are good on chatterbaits and creature baits. Black bass are slow around retaining walls and main lake points. Bass are deep on big crankbaits.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has picked up again on main lake wind blown points and tree lines with chatterbaits in 3-5 feet.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Black bass, crappie and white bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great on minnows and jigs around main lake brush piles have been best. Getting some reports of crappie around the U.S. Largemouth bass have been good early on topwater baits, then switch to finesse baits around cover and docks as the sun rises. Chartreuse slabs and live bait have been putting them in the boat.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 6.62 pounds are fair on Hag’s Cheat Codes in Ramsey’s revenge color, shaky heads and top waters in 2-10 feet of water. Crappie to 11 inches are good around docks on minnows and jigs in 10-15 feet. White bass are fair with catches ranging between 10-12 inches on crankbaits and crappie jigs with some topwater action early and late in the day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting on brush piles when it is overcast using jigs and crankbaits.
reports.by: The Bait Barn

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on rock piles with topwaters, swimbaits and crankbaits. reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Cast spinnerbaits and slabs and look for schooling fish close to seawalls and shorelines. Use spinnerbaits like a mepps#4 spinner or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Hit up seawalls close to points in depths of 7-12 feet and cast rattle traps, spoons or sassy shads to get the Hybrids to bite.The crappie bite has been getting increasingly better. Now that the water is receding target crappie with small jigs in 5-12 feet under bridge pylons or under docks.

reports.text: Crappie are good and relating to brush in 18-28 feet deep with some fish suspended mid depth minnows working best.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on slabs on main lake points and humps in 20 feet of water. Crappie are slow on minnows over brush piles in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Due to the rise in lake level there is a lot of submerged vegetation scattering the fish.Those anglers that like to flip brush for bass this is your time to shine. Small bass are biting off points with Carolina rigs and jigs. Some crappie are shallow in flooded brush, and in stand ups in 12-15 feet of water. Bass are shallow in flooded bushes and trees in 4-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good, and bluegill and catfish are fair in the marina. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows over brush in 10-20 feet water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on soft plastic baits in the brush along shorelines in 4- 12 feet of water.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow with three fish stringers up to 8 pounds. Very little crappie or catfish action on the water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Live bait and slabs are working well. The crappie have been fair on brush tops in 16 feet have been the ticket. Largemouth bass have been good at day light on frogs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is fair on brush piles in 15-20 feet of water near creeks and inflow. Use minnows on shallow rocky banks for black crappie. Bass fishing is fair fishing top waters early in the banks of creeks and along the edges of main lake points. Slab season is almost here. When we see bigger fish beneath the smaller fish feeding on the shad bring out the slabs.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing can be tough.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good using minnows on brush in 16 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been good in 5-15 feet of water with swimbaits and crankbaits. There is some bass up against the reeds biting small spinners and worms. Crappie fishing seems to be fair to good but it can be hard to get a limit of keeper size. Crappie are good in 15-18 feet of water in brush on minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good catching numbers and some quality as well. When the shad are thick in places/coves, we are catching good bass and hybrids mixed in as well. If it's Crappie you are after, we are catching those and huge bluegill and sunfish as well using crappie jugs and inline spinners.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 15-20 feet of water on senkos in the cooler areas of the lake.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be fair on small jigs and minnows in timber in 15-25 feet of water on the north end of the lake. Largemouth bass fishing is slow.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20-28 feet of water over brush with minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good with 2-4 pound catches in 10-30 feet of water near submerged tree limbs and shallow running points. Crappie fair.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with fish scattered on grass edges out to 12 feet with shaky head worms and jigs. Crappie have slowed down on brush, but fish are finicky on small jigs.
reports.by: Jim Brack, Athens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting from first light until about 9 a.m. then it seems to slow down quite a bit.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good on watermelon seed flukes, perch colored weightless, swimbaits, and creature baits in watermelon seed and pumpkin. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop. Bass are biting early in the morning in the discharge on shaky heads and small Carolina rigged super fluke juniors. Later in the day bass are moving to grass lines on the main lake hitting using flukes, worms and creature baits. Schooling bass action on small swimbaits and tiny clear topwaters.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with live minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush piles in 20-30 feet of water with jigs or minnows. Black bass are slow around retaining walls and main lake points.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to good on soft plastics, chatterbaits and minnows. Crappie and white bass slow, catfish good on live and cut bait on trotlines and jug lines, flatheads running late night with cut bait on rod and reel.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in the weeds on soft plastics.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 7.25 pounds are slow on jigs, shaky heads and top waters in 2-10 feet. Crappie to 11 inches are excellent under docks on minnows and jigs in 6-12 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow while the lake is flooded. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass can be caught on topwaters in the mornings, then a dropshot or neko rig on deeper grass.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Use spinnerbaits like a mepps #4 spinner or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Hit up seawalls close to points in depths of 7-12 feet and cast rattle traps, spoons or sassy shads to get the Hybrids to bite.The crappie bite has been getting increasingly better.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good in shallow water out to 10 feet using flukes and soft plastic worms, shad colored crankbaits. Crappie are good in brush piles in 20-30 feet of water on minnows or grubs.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.text: Bass should be off of vegetation on soft plastics.

reports.text: Crappie are slow. Largemouth are slow.
