reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush piles in 20 feet of water with jigs or minnows. Shad are spawning so bass can be caught along the banks on topwaters.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on main lake structures with slabs with teaser flies. Crappie are fair to good on brush piles and main lake structure on jigs with white color combinations.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good near the dam and in 8-15 feet of water on the ledges with Carolina rigged worms, and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on top waters frogs early in the morning over grass, and Yellow Magics along the edge of the grass Texas rigs and Carolina rigs good around bream beds 3-7 feet. Black bass are challenging with constant weather extremes, look for the clearest water you can find. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork was definitely moving into the steady summer pattern this week. We are still seeing great numbers of black crappie on lay downs and certain trees in 14-28 feet. You can also find black crappie on certain docks and bridges over the next few months. We have been seeing lots of small white crappie on brush piles but some bigger keepers showed up the last few days. Some summer time trees are…
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are near the water intake or near the dam on rocks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Small bass are abundant using dark natural live soft plastics in less than 4 feet of water.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Topwater action for striped bass, largemouth bass and white bass species has been occurring early and late. White bass are also good on Alabama rigs, rattle traps and slabs. Largemouth bass continue to be fair to good to 7 pounds near laydown structure and near main lake points or creek entrances. Crappie action is fair to good on small jigs or minnows fished around trees and bridge pilings mid lake from Ports-O-Call to the City Beach.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on spinnerbaits fished in shallow water. Crappie are good on 1/32 ounce jigs fished over cover in 8-15 feet of water. White bass are very good to 2 pounds on slab spoons fished over main lake humps.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greenbelt fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in standing timber and shallow along the shore.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass are in their summer pattern, try dropping baits at the edge of grass and slow moving streamers in shad colors.. Bead heads will tempt bream and bass.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are being caught in Luces Bayou in 8-15 feet of water in minnows and small jigs hanging tight to structure. Largemouth bass are in docks and riprap biting grubs and worms.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in shallow water off of rocks or standing timber. Bass should be off of vegetation on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught on topwaters, soft plastics out in mid depths, and a few on chatterbaits around boat docks and the bank.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: With the high water bass can still be found shallow in the grass. Crappie on deep brush piles and bridge piling.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 25-30 feet timber and brush. Bass are good on points and brush piles with jigs, Texas rigged worms, or dropshot.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow while the lake is flooded. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair to good on humps and points in 20-35 feet of water using slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 10-30 feet of water in brush piles, rock piles, stumps, standing timber, and laydowns with minnows. Bass are in 4-10 feet of water with crankbaits, spinnerbaits or dragging a soft plastic.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: The crappie are stacked up in 6-12 feet this week on brush piles and standing timber. Largemouth bass are still in 3 feet or less on Texas rigs, frogs, and jackhammer chatterbaits. Some largemouth bass have also moved back to the main lake brush, bulkheads, docks in 4-8 feet using Texas rig, and jackhammer chatterbaits for the deeper bass.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good using underspin swimbaits, senkos and redbug colored worms in the hydrilla. Crappie are good at railroad trestle and brush piles in 25 feet using minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good shallow along the edges of the shore and should start to transition to brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on soft plastic trick worms on a Carolina rig or dropshot, and deep diving crankbaits. Crappie are good using ⅛ ounce chartreuse and white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report

reports.text: Crappie population is good. Bass are excellent with numerous catches between 4-6 pounds. Crappie are fair on chartreuse crappie jigs and live minnows.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 8 pounds. Crappie are good on minnows in rivers with some limits 6-12 feet.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are very good for the deeper water fishermen with Live Scopes, and fair for conventional and night anglers. Bass are very good, especially working the flooded shorelines with creatures and frogs.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent on large swimbaits and trick worms on Carolina rigs. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Use live shad or small slabs and jigs white, and silver are good colors. Bass are good in 20-30 feet on trees and ledges near points with Carolina rigs, shaky heads, glide baits, deep crankbaits. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide Service.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with minnows 15-28 feet on brush with some fish suspended mid depth.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to get in a summer pattern relating to 15-25 feet on small jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on slabs on main lake points and humps in 20-30 feet of water. Crappie are slow with minnows over brush piles in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are scattered from flooded bushes and grass. Target bass in the flooded bushes and trees with soft plastics. Few bass are on points and creek Carolina rigs and crankbaits. Crappie continue to roam in open water. Crappie are best on brush in 12 feet of water, but while the lake level is high the brush piles are 16-18 feet deep. White bass on deeper points with slab spoons and little George’s. Bass are shallow in flooded bushes and trees in 4-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good, catfish and bluegill are fair on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black Bass are fair hitting red sparkle crankbaits and spinnerbaits in 6-10 feet off drop-offs. Crappie are good on the brush piles in 10-20 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Largemouth bass are fair but keep patience in the tackle box, along with soft plastics pitched into the reeds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is slow using jigs and minnows on brush piles near creeks in 15-20 feet of water using electronics. Bass fishing is slow as they continue to lower the lake levels and draw water off the banks.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report

reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in the marinas throwing flukes under the floats. Bass are not straying far from structure. Bass are not schooling. Lake Travis is continuing to produce bass.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: White bass busting on shad at daylight hitting topwaters, or slabs.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good and the most productive lure seems to be plastic worms. Crappie are good in 15-18 feet of water in brush on minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good in shallow water main lake points and fish are reported being caught on main lake structure on slabs. White bass are good on main lake structures on slabs with teaser flies. Crappie are fair to good on brush piles and main lake structure on jigs with white color combinations.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service
